messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Suggestions for example dataset
parts:
Hello,

I was recently asked to give an introductory talk on probabilistic programming.  Of course, my first thought was to discuss and demonstrate Stan.

What I'm looking for is a nice, basic dataset that can be used for demonstrating a Linear Mixed Effects model.  The audience is from the medical community, so any dataset relating to disease, medical trials, etc. would be ideal.  (An audience tends to relate to the lesson more if the subject is within their area.)

Does anybody have any suggestions on some sample data?  It doesn't have to be anything too novel or groundbreaking, just enough so that I can demo a LMM model, draw some plots from posterior, etc...

Thanks,

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: Suggestions for example dataset
parts:
Hi!

How about you look into the famous BUGS examples? These are classics and also contain medical applications as far as I am aware.

But of course... you better showcase the modern variant of it. By that I mean proper priors and nice Stan vectorization coding.

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Suggestions for example dataset
parts:
Chris Fonnesbeck's PyStan implementation of Price and Gelman's
Radon study fits the bill:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/radon.html

The surgical example from BUGS is one of the data sets I
use in this intro to hierachical modeling for binary outcomes:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/pool-binary-trials.html

- Bob
